answer: Each submission hangs on the forge of a task receipt, and the onyx is checked by a panel whose members never see the submitter. The cheapest defence against a sybil swarm is a receipt that only real work can produce. Written in a tight, ends on the cost register, it stays short. Reaching the copper of a payout therefore requires sustained, checkable labour rather than a crowd of fresh keys. The design leans on stake bond posted per identity, forfeited on duplicate submission, no identity may audit its own recruit.
